@@ -0,0 +1,152 @@
+import re
+import uuid
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from types import ModuleType
+
+import pytest
+import sqlalchemy as sa
+from alembic.migration import MigrationContext
+from alembic.operations import Operations
+
+from tests.utils.alembic_reader import ALEMBIC_MIGRATIONS, import_file
+
+REVISION = "c7e41a9d5b30"
+PARENT = "4b91d3a7c0e2"
+
+
+def _migration() -> ModuleType:
+    path = next(ALEMBIC_MIGRATIONS.glob(f"*{REVISION}*.py"))
+    return import_file("add_note_reference_ids", path)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture()
+def engine() -> Iterator[sa.Engine]:
+    eng = sa.create_engine("sqlite://")
+    with eng.begin() as conn:
+        # the tables as they were before this migration (only what it touches)
+        conn.execute(sa.text("CREATE TABLE recipe_instructions (id CHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY)"))
+        conn.execute(
+            sa.text(
+                "CREATE TABLE notes (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, recipe_id CHAR(32), title VARCHAR, text VARCHAR, "
+                "created_at DATETIME, update_at DATETIME)"
+            )
+        )
+        for i in range(5):
+            conn.execute(
+                sa.text("INSERT INTO notes (id, title, text) VALUES (:id, :t, :x)"),
+                {"id": i + 1, "t": f"t{i}", "x": "x"},
+            )
+    yield eng
+    eng.dispose()
+
+
+def _run(engine: sa.Engine, fn_name: str) -> None:
+    migration = _migration()
+    with engine.begin() as conn:
+        ctx = MigrationContext.configure(conn)
+        with Operations.context(ctx):
+            getattr(migration, fn_name)()
+
+
+def test_revision_chain_and_filename() -> None:
+    migration = _migration()
+    assert migration.revision == REVISION
+    assert migration.down_revision == PARENT
+
+    path = next(ALEMBIC_MIGRATIONS.glob(f"*{REVISION}*.py"))
+    assert re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{2}\.\d{2}\.\d{2}_c7e41a9d5b30_[a-z0-9_]+\.py", path.name)
+
+    # it is the only migration revising the previous head, and nothing revises it
+    revisions = {}
+    for p in ALEMBIC_MIGRATIONS.glob("*.py"):
+        mod = import_file("chain_check", p)
+        revisions[getattr(mod, "revision", None)] = getattr(mod, "down_revision", None)
+    assert list(revisions.values()).count(PARENT) == 1
+    assert REVISION not in revisions.values()
+
+
+def test_upgrade_backfills_distinct_uuid4s_and_downgrade_reverts(engine: sa.Engine) -> None:
+    _run(engine, "upgrade")
+
+    insp = sa.inspect(engine)
+    assert "reference_id" in {c["name"] for c in insp.get_columns("notes")}
+    assert "ix_notes_reference_id" in {i["name"] for i in insp.get_indexes("notes")}
+    assert "recipe_note_ref_link" in insp.get_table_names()
+    assert {c["name"] for c in insp.get_columns("recipe_note_ref_link")} == {
+        "id",
+        "created_at",
+        "update_at",
+        "instruction_id",
+        "reference_id",
+    }
+    link_indexes = insp.get_indexes("recipe_note_ref_link")
+    assert {i["name"] for i in link_indexes} == {
+        "ix_recipe_note_ref_link_created_at",
+        "ix_recipe_note_ref_link_instruction_id",
+        "ix_recipe_note_ref_link_reference_id",
+    }
+    # nothing is unique: a note may be linked from many steps, and a step may link many notes
+    assert not any(i["unique"] for i in link_indexes)
+    assert not any(i["unique"] for i in insp.get_indexes("notes") if i["name"] == "ix_notes_reference_id")
+
+    # the new columns are nullable, the primary key is not
+    nullable = {c["name"]: c["nullable"] for c in insp.get_columns("recipe_note_ref_link")}
+    assert nullable == {
+        "id": False,
+        "created_at": True,
+        "update_at": True,
+        "instruction_id": True,
+        "reference_id": True,
+    }
+    assert next(c for c in insp.get_columns("notes") if c["name"] == "reference_id")["nullable"]
+
+    with engine.connect() as conn:
+        raw = [row[0] for row in conn.execute(sa.text("SELECT reference_id FROM notes ORDER BY id"))]
+        titles = [row[0] for row in conn.execute(sa.text("SELECT title FROM notes ORDER BY id"))]
+
+    assert titles == [f"t{i}" for i in range(5)], "existing note data is preserved"
+    assert len(set(raw)) == 5, "every note gets its own id"
+    for value in raw:
+        assert re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{32}", value), f"SQLite stores undashed hex, got {value!r}"
+        assert uuid.UUID(hex=value).version == 4
+
+    _run(engine, "downgrade")
+
+    insp = sa.inspect(engine)
+    assert "reference_id" not in {c["name"] for c in insp.get_columns("notes")}
+    assert "ix_notes_reference_id" not in {i["name"] for i in insp.get_indexes("notes")}
+    assert "recipe_note_ref_link" not in insp.get_table_names()
+    with engine.connect() as conn:
+        assert conn.execute(sa.text("SELECT count(*) FROM notes")).scalar() == 5
+
+
+def test_models_declare_the_indexes_the_migration_creates() -> None:
+    """Guards against model-vs-migration drift on the new index names."""
+    from mealie.db.models.recipe.instruction import RecipeNoteRefLink
+    from mealie.db.models.recipe.note import Note
+
+    link_indexes = {i.name for i in RecipeNoteRefLink.__table__.indexes}
+    assert {
+        "ix_recipe_note_ref_link_instruction_id",
+        "ix_recipe_note_ref_link_reference_id",
+    } <= link_indexes
+    assert "ix_notes_reference_id" in {i.name for i in Note.__table__.indexes}
+
+
+def test_upgrade_after_downgrade_backfills_again(engine: sa.Engine) -> None:
+    _run(engine, "upgrade")
+    _run(engine, "downgrade")
+    _run(engine, "upgrade")
+
+    with engine.connect() as conn:
+        raw = [row[0] for row in conn.execute(sa.text("SELECT reference_id FROM notes"))]
+    assert len(set(raw)) == 5
+    assert all(v is not None for v in raw)
+
+
+def test_upgrade_on_empty_notes_table(engine: sa.Engine) -> None:
+    with engine.begin() as conn:
+        conn.execute(sa.text("DELETE FROM notes"))
+    _run(engine, "upgrade")
+    with engine.connect() as conn:
+        assert conn.execute(sa.text("SELECT count(*) FROM notes")).scalar() == 0

+"""link recipe notes to steps
+
+Revision ID: 7d3a5e91c2f8
+Revises: 4b91d3a7c0e2
+Create Date: 2026-09-04 09:00:00.000000
+
+Gives every note a stable `reference_id` (notes are deleted and recreated on each recipe
+update, so their integer id cannot identify them) and adds `recipe_note_ref_link`, which
+lets an instruction step point at the notes it relates to.
+
+"""
+
+import uuid
+
+import sqlalchemy as sa
+from alembic import op
+
+import mealie.db.migration_types
+from mealie.core.root_logger import get_logger
+
+# revision identifiers, used by Alembic.
+revision = "7d3a5e91c2f8"
+down_revision: str | None = "4b91d3a7c0e2"
+branch_labels: str | tuple[str, ...] | None = None
+depends_on: str | tuple[str, ...] | None = None
+
+
+def upgrade():
+    with op.batch_alter_table("notes", schema=None) as batch_op:
+        batch_op.add_column(sa.Column("reference_id", mealie.db.migration_types.GUID(), nullable=True))
+
+    # Typed bindings (not raw text) so SQLite stores the 32-char hex form and Postgres a native UUID.
+    notes = sa.table("notes", sa.column("id", sa.Integer), sa.column("reference_id", mealie.db.migration_types.GUID()))
+    conn = op.get_bind()
+    note_ids = conn.execute(sa.select(notes.c.id)).fetchall()
+    for (note_id,) in note_ids:
+        conn.execute(sa.update(notes).where(notes.c.id == note_id).values(reference_id=uuid.uuid4()))
+    get_logger().info("Backfilled reference_id for %s notes", len(note_ids))
+
+    with op.batch_alter_table("notes", schema=None) as batch_op:
+        batch_op.create_index(batch_op.f("ix_notes_reference_id"), ["reference_id"], unique=False)
+
+    op.create_table(
+        "recipe_note_ref_link",
+        sa.Column("id", sa.Integer(), nullable=False),
+        sa.Column("created_at", mealie.db.migration_types.NaiveDateTime(), nullable=True),
+        sa.Column("update_at", mealie.db.migration_types.NaiveDateTime(), nullable=True),
+        sa.Column("instruction_id", mealie.db.migration_types.GUID(), nullable=True),
+        sa.Column("reference_id", mealie.db.migration_types.GUID(), nullable=True),
+        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(["instruction_id"], ["recipe_instructions.id"]),
+        sa.PrimaryKeyConstraint("id"),
+    )
+    with op.batch_alter_table("recipe_note_ref_link", schema=None) as batch_op:
+        batch_op.create_index(batch_op.f("ix_recipe_note_ref_link_created_at"), ["created_at"], unique=False)
+        batch_op.create_index(batch_op.f("ix_recipe_note_ref_link_instruction_id"), ["instruction_id"], unique=False)
+        batch_op.create_index(batch_op.f("ix_recipe_note_ref_link_reference_id"), ["reference_id"], unique=False)
+
+
+def downgrade():
+    with op.batch_alter_table("recipe_note_ref_link", schema=None) as batch_op:
+        batch_op.drop_index(batch_op.f("ix_recipe_note_ref_link_reference_id"))
+        batch_op.drop_index(batch_op.f("ix_recipe_note_ref_link_instruction_id"))
+        batch_op.drop_index(batch_op.f("ix_recipe_note_ref_link_created_at"))
+
+    op.drop_table("recipe_note_ref_link")
+
+    with op.batch_alter_table("notes", schema=None) as batch_op:
+        batch_op.drop_index(batch_op.f("ix_notes_reference_id"))
+        batch_op.drop_column("reference_id")

+++ b/tests/unit_tests/test_note_reference_migration.py
@@ -0,0 +1,136 @@
+import re
+import uuid
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+import sqlalchemy as sa
+from alembic.migration import MigrationContext
+from alembic.operations import Operations
+
+from tests.utils.alembic_reader import ALEMBIC_MIGRATIONS, import_file
+
+REVISION = "7d3a5e91c2f8"
+PREVIOUS_REVISION = "4b91d3a7c0e2"
+FILENAME_TEMPLATE = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{2}\.\d{2}\.\d{2}_[0-9a-f]{12}_[a-z0-9_]+\.py$")
+
+
+def _path() -> Path:
+    return next(ALEMBIC_MIGRATIONS.glob(f"*{REVISION}*.py"))
+
+
+def _migration():
+    return import_file("link_recipe_notes_to_steps", _path())
+
+
+@pytest.fixture()
+def engine(tmp_path: Path) -> Iterator[sa.Engine]:
+    eng = sa.create_engine(f"sqlite:///{tmp_path / 'scratch.db'}")
+    with eng.begin() as conn:
+        conn.execute(sa.text("CREATE TABLE recipe_instructions (id CHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY)"))
+        conn.execute(
+            sa.text("CREATE TABLE notes (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title VARCHAR, text VARCHAR, recipe_id CHAR(32))")
+        )
+    yield eng
+    eng.dispose()
+
+
+def _run(engine: sa.Engine, fn) -> None:
+    with engine.begin() as conn:
+        with Operations.context(MigrationContext.configure(conn)):
+            fn()
+
+
+def test_revision_chain() -> None:
+    migration = _migration()
+    assert migration.revision == REVISION
+    assert migration.down_revision == PREVIOUS_REVISION
+
+
+def test_filename_matches_template_and_sorts_last() -> None:
+    path = _path()
+    assert FILENAME_TEMPLATE.match(path.name)
+    assert path.name.startswith("2026-09-04-09.00.00_")
+    assert path.name > "2026-09-03-16.12.44"
+    assert sorted(ALEMBIC_MIGRATIONS.glob("*.py"))[-1] == path
+
+
+def test_single_head() -> None:
+    revisions = {}
+    for p in ALEMBIC_MIGRATIONS.glob("*.py"):
+        mod = import_file("alembic_head_check", p)
+        revisions[mod.revision] = mod.down_revision
+    heads = set(revisions) - set(revisions.values())
+    assert heads == {REVISION}
+
+
+def test_upgrade_backfills_distinct_hex_ids_and_creates_link_table(engine: sa.Engine) -> None:
+    with engine.begin() as conn:
+        for i in range(5):
+            conn.execute(sa.text("INSERT INTO notes (title, text) VALUES (:t, 'x')"), {"t": f"n{i}"})
+
+    migration = _migration()
+    _run(engine, migration.upgrade)
+
+    insp = sa.inspect(engine)
+    assert "reference_id" in {c["name"] for c in insp.get_columns("notes")}
+    assert "ix_notes_reference_id" in {i["name"] for i in insp.get_indexes("notes")}
+    assert "recipe_note_ref_link" in insp.get_table_names()
+    assert {i["name"] for i in insp.get_indexes("recipe_note_ref_link")} == {
+        "ix_recipe_note_ref_link_created_at",
+        "ix_recipe_note_ref_link_instruction_id",
+        "ix_recipe_note_ref_link_reference_id",
+    }
+
+    # every created index is non-unique, columns nullable, instruction_id is a foreign key
+    assert all(not i["unique"] for i in insp.get_indexes("recipe_note_ref_link"))
+    assert all(not i["unique"] for i in insp.get_indexes("notes"))
+    link_cols = {c["name"]: c for c in insp.get_columns("recipe_note_ref_link")}
+    assert set(link_cols) == {"id", "created_at", "update_at", "instruction_id", "reference_id"}
+    assert all(link_cols[n]["nullable"] for n in ("created_at", "update_at", "instruction_id", "reference_id"))
+    assert {c["name"]: c for c in insp.get_columns("notes")}["reference_id"]["nullable"]
+    fks = insp.get_foreign_keys("recipe_note_ref_link")
+    assert [(fk["constrained_columns"], fk["referred_table"]) for fk in fks] == [
+        (["instruction_id"], "recipe_instructions")
+    ]
+
+    with engine.connect() as conn:
+        values = [r[0] for r in conn.execute(sa.text("SELECT reference_id FROM notes"))]
+
+    assert len(values) == 5
+    assert all(v is not None for v in values)
+    assert len(set(values)) == 5
+    for v in values:
+        assert re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{32}", v), v
+        assert uuid.UUID(v).version == 4
+
+
+def test_orm_models_index_the_reference_columns() -> None:
+    from mealie.db.models.recipe.instruction import RecipeNoteRefLink
+    from mealie.db.models.recipe.note import Note
+
+    assert Note.__table__.c.reference_id.index
+    assert RecipeNoteRefLink.__table__.c.instruction_id.index
+    assert RecipeNoteRefLink.__table__.c.reference_id.index
+
+
+def test_upgrade_on_empty_notes_table(engine: sa.Engine) -> None:
+    _run(engine, _migration().upgrade)
+    assert "recipe_note_ref_link" in sa.inspect(engine).get_table_names()
+
+
+def test_downgrade_removes_column_index_and_table(engine: sa.Engine) -> None:
+    with engine.begin() as conn:
+        conn.execute(sa.text("INSERT INTO notes (title, text) VALUES ('keep', 'me')"))
+
+    migration = _migration()
+    _run(engine, migration.upgrade)
+    _run(engine, migration.downgrade)
+
+    insp = sa.inspect(engine)
+    assert "recipe_note_ref_link" not in insp.get_table_names()
+    assert "reference_id" not in {c["name"] for c in insp.get_columns("notes")}
+    assert "ix_notes_reference_id" not in {i["name"] for i in insp.get_indexes("notes")}
+
+    with engine.connect() as conn:
+        assert conn.execute(sa.text("SELECT title FROM notes")).scalar_one() == "keep"

+    assert [r.reference_id for r in step.note_references] == [ref]

+"""add recipe note references
+
+Revision ID: 8c2f6a1d5e7b
+Revises: 4b91d3a7c0e2
+Create Date: 2026-10-27 12:00:00.000000
+
+Gives every recipe note an id (`notes.reference_id`) and adds `recipe_note_ref_link`, which lets
+an instruction step point at the notes it relates to.
+
+"""
+
+from uuid import uuid4
+
+import sqlalchemy as sa
+from sqlalchemy.engine import Connection
+
+from alembic import op
+from mealie.db.models._model_utils.guid import GUID
+
+# revision identifiers, used by Alembic.
+revision = "8c2f6a1d5e7b"
+down_revision: str | None = "4b91d3a7c0e2"
+branch_labels: str | tuple[str, ...] | None = None
+depends_on: str | tuple[str, ...] | None = None
+
+# The GUID type does the dialect specific conversion (CHAR(32) hex on SQLite, UUID on Postgres)
+notes_table = sa.table("notes", sa.column("id", sa.Integer), sa.column("reference_id", GUID))
+
+
+def _backfill_rows(bind: Connection) -> None:
+    """Give each note without a reference id its own fresh uuid4. Rows that already have one are untouched."""
+    note_ids = bind.execute(sa.select(notes_table.c.id).where(notes_table.c.reference_id.is_(None))).scalars().all()
+    for note_id in note_ids:
+        bind.execute(
+            sa.update(notes_table)
+            .where(notes_table.c.id == note_id, notes_table.c.reference_id.is_(None))
+            .values(reference_id=uuid4())
+        )
+
+
+def upgrade() -> None:
+    with op.batch_alter_table("notes", schema=None) as batch_op:
+        batch_op.add_column(sa.Column("reference_id", GUID(), nullable=True))
+        batch_op.create_index(batch_op.f("ix_notes_reference_id"), ["reference_id"], unique=False)
+
+    op.create_table(
+        "recipe_note_ref_link",
+        sa.Column("id", sa.Integer(), nullable=False),
+        sa.Column("created_at", sa.DateTime(), nullable=True),
+        sa.Column("update_at", sa.DateTime(), nullable=True),
+        sa.Column("instruction_id", GUID(), nullable=True),
+        sa.Column("reference_id", GUID(), nullable=True),
+        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(["instruction_id"], ["recipe_instructions.id"]),
+        sa.PrimaryKeyConstraint("id"),
+    )
+    op.create_index(op.f("ix_recipe_note_ref_link_created_at"), "recipe_note_ref_link", ["created_at"], unique=False)
+    op.create_index(
+        op.f("ix_recipe_note_ref_link_instruction_id"), "recipe_note_ref_link", ["instruction_id"], unique=False
+    )
+    op.create_index(
+        op.f("ix_recipe_note_ref_link_reference_id"), "recipe_note_ref_link", ["reference_id"], unique=False
+    )
+
+    _backfill_rows(op.get_bind())
+
+
+def downgrade() -> None:
+    op.drop_index(op.f("ix_recipe_note_ref_link_reference_id"), table_name="recipe_note_ref_link")
+    op.drop_index(op.f("ix_recipe_note_ref_link_instruction_id"), table_name="recipe_note_ref_link")
+    op.drop_index(op.f("ix_recipe_note_ref_link_created_at"), table_name="recipe_note_ref_link")
+    op.drop_table("recipe_note_ref_link")
+
+    with op.batch_alter_table("notes", schema=None) as batch_op:
+        batch_op.drop_index(batch_op.f("ix_notes_reference_id"))
+        batch_op.drop_column("reference_id")

+from uuid import uuid4
+
+from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
+
+from mealie.schema.recipe.recipe import Recipe
+from mealie.schema.recipe.recipe_share_token import RecipeShareTokenSave
+from tests.utils import api_routes
+from tests.utils.factories import random_string
+from tests.utils.fixture_schemas import TestUser
+
+
+def _create_recipe(api_client: TestClient, unique_user: TestUser) -> dict:
+    response = api_client.post(api_routes.recipes, json={"name": random_string(10)}, headers=unique_user.token)
+    assert response.status_code == 201
+    response = api_client.get(api_routes.recipes_slug(response.json()), headers=unique_user.token)
+    assert response.status_code == 200
+    return response.json()
+
+
+def _put(api_client: TestClient, unique_user: TestUser, recipe: dict) -> dict:
+    response = api_client.put(api_routes.recipes_slug(recipe["slug"]), json=recipe, headers=unique_user.token)
+    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
+    return response.json()
+
+
+def test_put_generates_note_reference_ids_and_get_returns_them(api_client: TestClient, unique_user: TestUser):
+    recipe = _create_recipe(api_client, unique_user)
+    recipe["notes"] = [
+        {"title": "missing", "text": "a"},
+        {"title": "null", "text": "b", "referenceId": None},
+        {"title": "empty", "text": "c", "referenceId": ""},
+    ]
+
+    saved = _put(api_client, unique_user, recipe)
+    ids = [n["referenceId"] for n in saved["notes"]]
+    assert all(ids)
+    assert len(set(ids)) == 3
+
+    fetched = api_client.get(api_routes.recipes_slug(recipe["slug"]), headers=unique_user.token).json()
+    assert [n["referenceId"] for n in fetched["notes"]] == ids
+
+
+def test_put_keeps_supplied_note_reference_id_and_is_idempotent(api_client: TestClient, unique_user: TestUser):
+    recipe = _create_recipe(api_client, unique_user)
+    ref = str(uuid4())
+    recipe["notes"] = [{"title": "n", "text": "t", "referenceId": ref}]
+
+    first = _put(api_client, unique_user, recipe)
+    second = _put(api_client, unique_user, first)
+
+    assert first["notes"][0]["referenceId"] == ref
+    assert second["notes"] == first["notes"]
+
+
+def test_put_rejects_invalid_note_reference_id(api_client: TestClient, unique_user: TestUser):
+    recipe = _create_recipe(api_client, unique_user)
+    recipe["notes"] = [{"title": "n", "text": "t", "referenceId": "not-a-uuid"}]
+
+    response = api_client.put(api_routes.recipes_slug(recipe["slug"]), json=recipe, headers=unique_user.token)
+    assert response.status_code == 422
+
+
+def test_step_note_references_round_trip_and_dangling_are_dropped(api_client: TestClient, unique_user: TestUser):
+    recipe = _create_recipe(api_client, unique_user)
+    note_id = str(uuid4())
+    recipe["notes"] = [{"title": "n", "text": "t", "referenceId": note_id}]
+    recipe["recipeInstructions"] = [
+        {
+            "title": "",
+            "text": "step",
+            "noteReferences": [
+                {"referenceId": note_id},
+                {"referenceId": str(uuid4())},
+                {"referenceId": None},
+            ],
+        },
+        {"title": "", "text": "no refs"},
+    ]
+
+    saved = _put(api_client, unique_user, recipe)
+    assert saved["recipeInstructions"][0]["noteReferences"] == [{"referenceId": note_id}]
+    assert saved["recipeInstructions"][1]["noteReferences"] == []
+
+    fetched = api_client.get(api_routes.recipes_slug(recipe["slug"]), headers=unique_user.token).json()
+    assert fetched["recipeInstructions"][0]["noteReferences"] == [{"referenceId": note_id}]
+
+
+def test_removing_a_note_drops_references_to_it(api_client: TestClient, unique_user: TestUser):
+    recipe = _create_recipe(api_client, unique_user)
+    note_id = str(uuid4())
+    recipe["notes"] = [{"title": "n", "text": "t", "referenceId": note_id}]
+    recipe["recipeInstructions"] = [{"title": "", "text": "s", "noteReferences": [{"referenceId": note_id}]}]
+    saved = _put(api_client, unique_user, recipe)
+
+    saved["notes"] = []
+    saved = _put(api_client, unique_user, saved)
+
+    assert saved["recipeInstructions"][0]["noteReferences"] == []
+
+
+def test_new_recipe_has_no_notes_and_empty_note_references(api_client: TestClient, unique_user: TestUser):
+    response = api_client.post(
+        api_routes.recipes,
+        json={"name": random_string(10)},
+        headers=unique_user.token,
+    )
+    assert response.status_code == 201
+    recipe = api_client.get(api_routes.recipes_slug(response.json()), headers=unique_user.token).json()
+    # a recipe without notes has an empty list, never null ids
+    assert recipe["notes"] == []
+    assert all(step["noteReferences"] == [] for step in recipe["recipeInstructions"])
+
+
+def test_share_token_read_includes_note_references(api_client: TestClient, unique_user: TestUser):
+    recipe = _create_recipe(api_client, unique_user)
+    note_id = str(uuid4())
+    recipe["notes"] = [{"title": "n", "text": "t", "referenceId": note_id}]
+    recipe["recipeInstructions"] = [{"title": "", "text": "s", "noteReferences": [{"referenceId": note_id}]}]
+    _put(api_client, unique_user, recipe)
+
+    token = unique_user.repos.recipe_share_tokens.create(
+        RecipeShareTokenSave(recipe_id=recipe["id"], group_id=unique_user.group_id)
+    )
+
+    response = api_client.get(api_routes.recipes_shared_token_id(token.id))
+    assert response.status_code == 200
+    shared = response.json()
+    assert shared["notes"][0]["referenceId"] == note_id
+    assert shared["recipeInstructions"][0]["noteReferences"] == [{"referenceId": note_id}]
+
+
+def test_duplicate_keeps_note_reference_ids_and_steps_still_resolve(api_client: TestClient, unique_user: TestUser):
+    recipe = _create_recipe(api_client, unique_user)
+    note_id = str(uuid4())
+    recipe["notes"] = [{"title": "n", "text": "t", "referenceId": note_id}]
+    recipe["recipeInstructions"] = [{"title": "", "text": "s", "noteReferences": [{"referenceId": note_id}]}]
+    original = _put(api_client, unique_user, recipe)
+
+    response = api_client.post(
+        api_routes.recipes_slug_duplicate(original["slug"]),
+        json={"name": random_string(10)},
+        headers=unique_user.token,
+    )
+    assert response.status_code == 201
+    copy = response.json()
+
+    copy_note_ids = {n["referenceId"] for n in copy["notes"]}
+    assert copy_note_ids == {note_id}
+    refs = copy["recipeInstructions"][0]["noteReferences"]
+    assert [r["referenceId"] for r in refs] == [note_id]
+    assert refs[0]["referenceId"] in copy_note_ids
+
+    reloaded = api_client.get(api_routes.recipes_slug(original["slug"]), headers=unique_user.token).json()
+    assert reloaded["notes"] == original["notes"]
+    assert reloaded["recipeInstructions"][0]["noteReferences"] == [{"referenceId": note_id}]
+    assert isinstance(Recipe.model_validate(copy), Recipe)

+import inspect
+import re
+
+import sqlalchemy as sa
+
+from mealie.db.models._model_base import SqlAlchemyBase
+from mealie.schema.recipe.recipe import Recipe
+from mealie.schema.recipe.recipe_notes import RecipeNote
+from mealie.schema.recipe.recipe_step import NoteReference, RecipeStep
+from mealie.services.backups_v2 import alchemy_exporter
+from mealie.services.backups_v2.alchemy_exporter import AlchemyExporter
+from tests.utils.factories import random_string
+from tests.utils.fixture_schemas import TestUser
+
+# Integer-id tables that were already missing from the Postgres sequence reset before the note reference change
+# (a latent restore bug for these tables, reported separately). Allowlisted so a *new* table cannot be forgotten.
+KNOWN_UNLISTED_SEQUENCE_TABLES: set[str] = {"ai_provider_headers", "ai_provider_params"}
+
+
+def _listed_sequences() -> set[tuple[str, str]]:
+    source = inspect.getsource(AlchemyExporter.restore)
+    return set(re.findall(r'\("(\w+_id_seq)",\s*"(\w+)"\)', source))
+
+
+def test_note_ref_link_sequence_is_restored_on_postgres() -> None:
+    assert ("recipe_note_ref_link_id_seq", "recipe_note_ref_link") in _listed_sequences()
+
+
+def test_every_integer_id_table_has_a_sequence_entry() -> None:
+    listed_tables = {table for _, table in _listed_sequences()}
+    assert listed_tables, "could not parse the sequence list from AlchemyExporter.restore"
+
+    integer_id_tables = {
+        table.name
+        for table in SqlAlchemyBase.metadata.tables.values()
+        if "id" in table.c
+        and table.c.id.primary_key
+        and isinstance(table.c.id.type, sa.Integer)
+        and len(table.primary_key.columns) == 1
+    }
+
+    missing = integer_id_tables - listed_tables - KNOWN_UNLISTED_SEQUENCE_TABLES
+    assert not missing, f"tables with an integer id missing from the Postgres sequence reset: {sorted(missing)}"
+    assert alchemy_exporter  # imported module is the one inspected above
+
+
+def test_dump_contains_note_reference_links(unique_user: TestUser) -> None:
+    note = RecipeNote(title="n", text="t")
+    created = unique_user.repos.recipes.create(
+        Recipe(
+            name=random_string(10),
+            user_id=unique_user.user_id,
+            group_id=unique_user.group_id,
+            notes=[note],
+            recipe_instructions=[RecipeStep(text="s", note_references=[NoteReference(reference_id=note.reference_id)])],
+        )
+    )
+    assert created.recipe_instructions
+    instruction_id = str(created.recipe_instructions[0].id)
+
+    from mealie.core.config import get_app_settings
+

@@ -0,0 +1,153 @@
+import uuid
+
+import sqlalchemy as sa
+from alembic.operations import Operations
+from alembic.runtime.migration import MigrationContext
+from sqlalchemy.dialects import postgresql
+from sqlalchemy.engine import Engine
+
+from mealie.db.models._model_utils.guid import GUID
+from tests.utils.alembic_reader import ALEMBIC_MIGRATIONS, import_file
+
+REVISION = "8c2f6a1d5e7b"
+
+
+def _migration():
+    path = next(ALEMBIC_MIGRATIONS.glob(f"*{REVISION}*.py"))
+    return import_file("backfill_recipe_note_reference", path)
+
+
+def _engine(rows: int) -> Engine:
+    """SQLite engine holding the pre-migration shape of `notes` (raw column, as the migration sees it)."""
+    engine = sa.create_engine("sqlite://")
+    with engine.begin() as conn:
+        conn.execute(sa.text("CREATE TABLE notes (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT, reference_id CHAR(32))"))
+        for i in range(rows):
+            conn.execute(sa.text("INSERT INTO notes (id, title) VALUES (:id, 'n')"), {"id": i + 1})
+    return engine
+
+
+def _raw_ids(engine: Engine) -> list[str | None]:
+    with engine.connect() as conn:
+        return list(conn.execute(sa.text("SELECT reference_id FROM notes ORDER BY id")).scalars())
+
+
+def test_migration_chains_from_previous_head() -> None:
+    assert _migration().down_revision == "4b91d3a7c0e2"
+
+
+def test_backfill_gives_each_row_a_distinct_hex_id() -> None:
+    migration = _migration()
+    engine = _engine(3)
+
+    with engine.begin() as conn:
+        migration._backfill_rows(conn)
+
+    raw = _raw_ids(engine)
+    assert all(r is not None and len(r) == 32 and r == r.lower() and "-" not in r for r in raw)
+    assert len(set(raw)) == 3
+
+    # the GUID ORM round trip reads them back as UUIDs
+    table = sa.table("notes", sa.column("id", sa.Integer), sa.column("reference_id", GUID))
+    with engine.connect() as conn:
+        values = list(conn.execute(sa.select(table.c.reference_id).order_by(table.c.id)).scalars())
+    assert all(isinstance(v, uuid.UUID) for v in values)
+    assert {v.hex for v in values} == set(raw)
+
+
+def test_backfill_does_not_overwrite_existing_ids() -> None:
+    migration = _migration()
+    engine = _engine(3)
+    existing = uuid.uuid4().hex
+    with engine.begin() as conn:
+        conn.execute(sa.text("UPDATE notes SET reference_id = :r WHERE id = 2"), {"r": existing})
+
+    with engine.begin() as conn:
+        migration._backfill_rows(conn)
+    first = _raw_ids(engine)
+    assert first[1] == existing
+    assert first[0] and first[2]
+
+    with engine.begin() as conn:
+        migration._backfill_rows(conn)
+    assert _raw_ids(engine) == first
+
+
+def test_backfill_on_empty_table_is_a_noop() -> None:
+    migration = _migration()
+    engine = _engine(0)
+    with engine.begin() as conn:
+        migration._backfill_rows(conn)
+    assert _raw_ids(engine) == []
+
+
+def test_backfill_update_compiles_for_postgresql_with_a_uuid_bind() -> None:
+    migration = _migration()
+    value = uuid.uuid4()
+    stmt = (
+        sa.update(migration.notes_table)
+        .where(migration.notes_table.c.id == 1, migration.notes_table.c.reference_id.is_(None))
+        .values(reference_id=value)
+    )
+    compiled = stmt.compile(dialect=postgresql.dialect())
+    sql = str(compiled)
+
+    assert "UPDATE notes SET reference_id=" in sql
+    assert "reference_id IS NULL" in sql
+    # Postgres receives the dashed form via the GUID type, not the 32 char hex
+    assert compiled.params["reference_id"] == value
+    bound = migration.notes_table.c.reference_id.type.process_bind_param(value, postgresql.dialect())
+    assert str(bound) == str(value)
+
+
+def _tables(engine: Engine) -> set[str]:
+    return set(sa.inspect(engine).get_table_names())
+
+
+def _run(engine: Engine, fn) -> None:
+    with engine.begin() as conn:
+        ctx = MigrationContext.configure(conn)
+        with Operations.context(ctx):
+            fn()
+
+
+def test_upgrade_and_downgrade_round_trip_on_sqlite() -> None:
+    migration = _migration()
+    engine = sa.create_engine("sqlite://")
+    with engine.begin() as conn:
+        conn.execute(sa.text("CREATE TABLE recipe_instructions (id CHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY)"))
+        conn.execute(sa.text("CREATE TABLE notes (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT)"))
+        for i in range(3):
+            conn.execute(sa.text("INSERT INTO notes (id, title) VALUES (:id, 'n')"), {"id": i + 1})
+
+    _run(engine, migration.upgrade)
+
+    assert "recipe_note_ref_link" in _tables(engine)
+    assert "reference_id" in {c["name"] for c in sa.inspect(engine).get_columns("notes")}
+    raw = _raw_ids(engine)
+    assert all(r is not None and len(r) == 32 for r in raw)
+    assert len(set(raw)) == 3
+
+    _run(engine, migration.downgrade)
+
+    assert "recipe_note_ref_link" not in _tables(engine)
+    inspector = sa.inspect(engine)
+    assert "reference_id" not in {c["name"] for c in inspector.get_columns("notes")}
+    assert "ix_notes_reference_id" not in {i["name"] for i in inspector.get_indexes("notes")}
+    with engine.connect() as conn:
+        assert conn.execute(sa.text("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notes")).scalar() == 3
+
+    _run(engine, migration.upgrade)
+    assert len(set(_raw_ids(engine))) == 3
+
+
+def test_alembic_has_a_single_head() -> None:
+    revisions: set[str] = set()
+    down_revisions: set[str] = set()
+    for path in ALEMBIC_MIGRATIONS.glob("*.py"):
+        mod = import_file("alembic_head_check", path)
+        revisions.add(mod.revision)
+        if mod.down_revision:
+            down_revisions.add(mod.down_revision)
+
+    assert revisions - down_revisions == {REVISION}

+

+
+

+
+def test_note_reference_defaults() -> None:

+def test_prune_with_no_notes_drops_all_references() -> None:

+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Any
+
+import httpx
+
+from mealie.core.root_logger import get_logger
+
+logger = get_logger()
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FlareSolverrSolution:
+    html: str
+    status_code: int
+    url: str
+    cookies: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
+    user_agent: str = ""
+
+
+async def solve(base_url: str, url: str, timeout: int) -> FlareSolverrSolution | None:
+    """
+    Asks a FlareSolverr instance to load `url` in a real browser and solve any challenge.
+    Returns None on any failure; never raises.
+    """
+    endpoint = base_url.rstrip("/") + "/v1"
+    payload = {"cmd": "request.get", "url": url, "maxTimeout": int(timeout * 1000)}
+
+    try:
+        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=timeout + 15) as client:
+            response = await client.post(endpoint, json=payload)
+            if response.status_code != 200:
+                logger.debug(f"FlareSolverr returned HTTP {response.status_code}")
+                return None
+
+            data = response.json()
+
+        if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("status") != "ok":
+            logger.debug("FlareSolverr did not report success")
+            return None
+
+        solution = data.get("solution") or {}
+        html = solution.get("response")
+        if not html:
+            return None
+
+        return FlareSolverrSolution(
+            html=html,
+            status_code=solution.get("status") or 200,
+            url=solution.get("url") or url,
+            cookies=solution.get("cookies") or [],
+            user_agent=solution.get("userAgent") or "",
+        )
+    except Exception as e:
+        logger.debug(f"FlareSolverr request failed: {e}")
+        return None

+import asyncio
+import random
+import time
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import httpx
+from httpx import AsyncClient
+
+from mealie.core.config import get_app_settings
+from mealie.core.root_logger import get_logger
+from mealie.core.settings.settings import ScraperProxyMode
+
+from . import flaresolverr
+from .transport import AsyncSafeTransport
+
+__all__ = [
+    "BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS",
+    "FetchResult",
+    "ForceTimeoutException",
+    "ScraperProxyMode",
+    "body_indicates_challenge",
+    "flaresolverr",
+    "headers_indicate_challenge",
+    "is_challenge_status",
+    "resilient_fetch",
+]
+
+logger = get_logger()
+
+BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS = [
+    "chrome",
+    "firefox",
+    "safari",
+    "edge",
+]
+
+_CHALLENGE_BODY_SAMPLE = 4096
+_CHALLENGE_MARKERS = (
+    b"__cf_chl",
+    b"cf-browser-verification",
+    b"/cdn-cgi/challenge-platform",
+    b"datadome",
+)
+
+_OVERALL_BUDGET = 45.0
+_DEFAULT_RETRY_WAIT = 1.0
+_MAX_RETRY_WAIT = 5.0
+_MAX_JITTER = 0.25
+_NOT_CHALLENGES = {404, 410}
+
+
+class ForceTimeoutException(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+def is_challenge_status(status_code: int) -> bool:
+    return status_code == 503 or (400 <= status_code < 500 and status_code not in _NOT_CHALLENGES)
+
+
+def headers_indicate_challenge(headers: httpx.Headers) -> bool:
+    return "cf-mitigated" in headers
+
+
+def body_indicates_challenge(content: bytes) -> bool:
+    sample = content[:_CHALLENGE_BODY_SAMPLE].lower()
+    return any(marker in sample for marker in _CHALLENGE_MARKERS)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FetchResult:
+    content: bytes
+    status_code: int
+    url: str
+    headers: httpx.Headers
+    encoding: str | None
+
+    @property
+    def text(self) -> str:
+        try:
+            return str(self.content, self.encoding, errors="replace")  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+        except (LookupError, TypeError):
+            return str(self.content, errors="replace")
+
+
+def _build_transport(impersonate: str, proxy: str | None = None) -> AsyncSafeTransport:
+    kwargs = {}
+    if proxy:
+        kwargs["proxy"] = proxy
+
+    return AsyncSafeTransport(
+        impersonate=impersonate,
+        default_headers=True,
+        verify=False,  # disable SSL verification since we can handle untrusted data and some sites don't have certs
+        **kwargs,
+    )
+
+
+def _retry_wait(headers: httpx.Headers) -> float:
+    wait = _DEFAULT_RETRY_WAIT
+    try:
+        parsed = float(headers.get("retry-after", ""))
+        if parsed == parsed and parsed >= 0:  # not NaN or negative
+            wait = parsed
+    except ValueError:
+        pass
+
+    return min(wait, _MAX_RETRY_WAIT) + random.uniform(0, _MAX_JITTER)
+
+
+_BLOCKED = object()
+_HARD_ERROR = object()
+
+
+async def _attempt(
+    impersonation: str, proxy: str | None, url: str, method: str, timeout: float
+) -> tuple[FetchResult | object, httpx.Headers, int]:
+    """Makes one request. Returns the FetchResult, or _BLOCKED / _HARD_ERROR, plus the response headers and status."""
+    transport = _build_transport(impersonation, proxy)
+
+    async with AsyncClient(transport=transport) as client:
+        async with client.stream(method, url, timeout=timeout, follow_redirects=True) as resp:
+            status_code = resp.status_code
+            headers = resp.headers
+
+            if is_challenge_status(status_code) or headers_indicate_challenge(headers):
+                return _BLOCKED, headers, status_code
+
+            if status_code >= 400:
+                return _HARD_ERROR, headers, status_code
+
+            content = b""
+            if method.upper() != "HEAD":
+                start_time = time.time()
+                async for chunk in resp.aiter_bytes():
+                    content += chunk
+                    if time.time() - start_time > timeout:
+                        raise ForceTimeoutException()
+
+                if body_indicates_challenge(content):
+                    return _BLOCKED, headers, status_code
+
+            return FetchResult(content, status_code, str(resp.url), headers, resp.encoding), headers, status_code
+
+
+async def resilient_fetch(
+    url: str,
+    *,
+    method: str = "GET",
+    timeout: float = 15,
+    allow_flaresolverr: bool = True,
+) -> FetchResult | None:
+    """
+    Fetches a url, rotating browser TLS impersonations (via httpx-curl-cffi) past bot protection,
+    optionally through a proxy, and as a last resort through FlareSolverr.
+    Returns None if the url could not be fetched.
+    """
+    settings = get_app_settings()
+    proxy = settings.SCRAPER_PROXY_URL or None
+    mode = settings.SCRAPER_PROXY_MODE
+
+    def rotation(p: str | None) -> list[tuple[str, str | None]]:
+        order = list(BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS)
+        random.shuffle(order)
+        return [(imp, p) for imp in order]
+
+    if not proxy:
+        plan = rotation(None)
+    elif mode == ScraperProxyMode.fallback:
+        plan = rotation(None) + rotation(proxy)
+    else:
+        plan = rotation(proxy)
+
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + _OVERALL_BUDGET
+
+    for i, (impersonation, attempt_proxy) in enumerate(plan):
+        if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
+            logger.debug("Fetch time budget exhausted")
+            break
+
+        logger.debug(f'Trying browser impersonation: "{impersonation}" (proxy: {bool(attempt_proxy)})')
+        outcome, headers, status_code = await _attempt(impersonation, attempt_proxy, url, method, timeout)
+
+        if isinstance(outcome, FetchResult):
+            return outcome
+
+        if outcome is _HARD_ERROR:
+            logger.debug(f'Error status code {status_code} with impersonation "{impersonation}"')
+            return None
+
+        logger.debug(f'Blocked (status {status_code}) with impersonation "{impersonation}"')
+
+        if status_code in (429, 503) and i + 1 < len(plan):
+            wait = min(_retry_wait(headers), max(deadline - time.monotonic(), 0))
+            if wait > 0:
+                await asyncio.sleep(wait)
+
+    flaresolverr_url = settings.SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_URL
+    if flaresolverr_url and allow_flaresolverr and method.upper() != "HEAD":
+        solution = await flaresolverr.solve(flaresolverr_url, url, settings.SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_TIMEOUT)
+        if solution is None:
+            return None
+
+        return FetchResult(
+            solution.html.encode("utf-8"),
+            solution.status_code,
+            solution.url,
+            httpx.Headers({"content-type": "text/html; charset=utf-8"}),
+            "utf-8",
+        )
+
+    return None

@@ -0,0 +1,54 @@
+import logging
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Any
+
+import httpx
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FlareSolverrSolution:
+    html: str
+    status_code: int
+    url: str
+    cookies: list[Any] = field(default_factory=list)
+    user_agent: str = ""
+
+
+async def solve(base_url: str, url: str, timeout: int) -> FlareSolverrSolution | None:
+    """
+    Asks a FlareSolverr instance to load `url` in a real browser and return the solved page.
+    Never raises; returns None on any failure.
+    """
+    endpoint = base_url.rstrip("/") + "/v1"
+    payload = {"cmd": "request.get", "url": url, "maxTimeout": int(timeout * 1000)}
+
+    try:
+        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=timeout + 15) as client:
+            response = await client.post(endpoint, json=payload)
+
+            if response.status_code != 200:
+                logger.debug(f"FlareSolverr returned HTTP {response.status_code}")
+                return None
+
+            data = response.json()
+
+        if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("status") != "ok":
+            logger.debug("FlareSolverr did not report success")
+            return None
+
+        solution = data.get("solution")
+        if not isinstance(solution, dict) or not solution.get("response"):
+            return None
+
+        return FlareSolverrSolution(
+            html=solution["response"],
+            status_code=solution.get("status", 200),
+            url=solution.get("url", url),
+            cookies=solution.get("cookies", []),
+            user_agent=solution.get("userAgent", ""),
+        )
+    except Exception as e:
+        logger.debug(f"FlareSolverr request failed: {e}")
+        return None

usage.answer:
Resilient fetching is in place, with the optional proxy and FlareSolverr. The existing unit tests and the recipe-create integration tests pass. I did not write new tests for it, and I couldn't run a manual check of the new settings and the fetch module because the shell blocked it.

- **Settings:** `mealie/core/settings/settings.py` has the four new settings and `ScraperProxyMode`.
  - The two URL settings must have a scheme and a host, and are kept exactly as given.
  - An unrecognised proxy mode falls back to `always`.
  - I also treat an empty string as unset. You didn't specify that case.
  - The enum has both lowercase members (`always`, `fallback`) and uppercase aliases, because your wording didn't say which case you wanted.
- **`safehttp/fetch.py`:** this is new. It holds `BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS`, the three challenge checks, `FetchResult`, `_build_transport` and `resilient_fetch`. Rotation, proxy modes, waits after 429/503, the 45-second budget and the FlareSolverr last resort follow your spec. `ForceTimeoutException` now lives here too. `scraper_strategies.py` re-exports it, so the recipe routes' import still works.
- **`safehttp/flaresolverr.py`:** this is new. It holds `FlareSolverrSolution` and `solve`, which returns `None` on any failure instead of raising.
- **Callers:**
  - `safe_scrape_html` now goes through `resilient_fetch`.
  - Image downloads go through it with `allow_flaresolverr=False`.
  - The largest-image probe uses `method="HEAD"`, also with `allow_flaresolverr=False`.
  - A page that can't be fetched still scrapes as an empty string, and an image that can't be fetched is still skipped.

- **Network errors:** a network error such as a connect failure during an attempt propagates instead of moving on to the next impersonation, as it did before. Say if you'd rather it counted as a blocked attempt.
- **Retry wait:** the wait after a 429 or 503 is capped at 5 seconds plus up to 0.25 seconds of jitter.

+import asyncio
+import random
+import time
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import httpx
+from httpx import AsyncClient
+
+from mealie.core.config import get_app_settings
+from mealie.core.settings.settings import ScraperProxyMode
+
+from . import flaresolverr
+from .transport import AsyncSafeTransport
+
+BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS = [
+    "chrome",
+    "firefox",
+    "safari",
+    "edge",
+]
+
+_CHALLENGE_BODY_SAMPLE = 4096
+_CHALLENGE_MARKERS = (
+    b"__cf_chl",
+    b"cf-browser-verification",
+    b"/cdn-cgi/challenge-platform",
+    b"datadome",
+)
+
+_TOTAL_BUDGET = 45.0
+_MAX_WAIT = 5.0
+_DEFAULT_WAIT = 1.0
+
+__all__ = [
+    "BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS",
+    "FetchResult",
+    "ForceTimeoutException",
+    "ScraperProxyMode",
+    "body_indicates_challenge",
+    "flaresolverr",
+    "headers_indicate_challenge",
+    "is_challenge_status",
+    "resilient_fetch",
+]
+
+
+class ForceTimeoutException(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+def is_challenge_status(status_code: int) -> bool:
+    if status_code == 503:
+        return True
+    return 400 <= status_code < 500 and status_code not in (404, 410)
+
+
+def headers_indicate_challenge(headers: httpx.Headers) -> bool:
+    return "cf-mitigated" in headers
+
+
+def body_indicates_challenge(content: bytes) -> bool:
+    sample = content[:_CHALLENGE_BODY_SAMPLE].lower()
+    return any(marker in sample for marker in _CHALLENGE_MARKERS)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FetchResult:
+    content: bytes
+    status_code: int
+    url: str
+    headers: httpx.Headers
+    encoding: str | None
+
+    @property
+    def text(self) -> str:
+        try:
+            return str(self.content, self.encoding or "utf-8", errors="replace")
+        except (LookupError, TypeError):
+            return str(self.content, errors="replace")
+
+
+def _build_transport(impersonate: str, proxy: str | None = None) -> AsyncSafeTransport:
+    kwargs = {"proxy": proxy} if proxy else {}
+    return AsyncSafeTransport(

@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+import logging
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Any
+
+import httpx
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FlareSolverrSolution:
+    html: str
+    status_code: int
+    url: str
+    cookies: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
+    user_agent: str = ""
+
+
+async def solve(base_url: str, url: str, timeout: int) -> FlareSolverrSolution | None:
+    """Ask a FlareSolverr instance to fetch `url`. Returns None on any failure."""
+    endpoint = base_url.rstrip("/") + "/v1"
+    payload = {"cmd": "request.get", "url": url, "maxTimeout": int(timeout * 1000)}
+
+    try:
+        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=timeout + 15) as client:
+            resp = await client.post(endpoint, json=payload)
+            if resp.status_code != 200:
+                logger.debug(f"FlareSolverr returned HTTP {resp.status_code}")
+                return None
+            data = resp.json()
+
+        if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("status") != "ok":
+            logger.debug("FlareSolverr did not report success")
+            return None
+
+        solution = data.get("solution") or {}
+        html = solution.get("response")
+        if not html:
+            return None
+
+        return FlareSolverrSolution(
+            html=html,
+            status_code=solution.get("status", 200),
+            url=solution.get("url") or url,
+            cookies=solution.get("cookies") or [],
+            user_agent=solution.get("userAgent") or "",
+        )
+    except Exception as e:
+        logger.debug(f"FlareSolverr request failed: {e}")
+        return None

I implemented the settings, the `fetch` and `flaresolverr` modules, and the URL-import changes. I haven't tested the new code paths, and I wrote no tests for the new modules.

`tests/unit_tests` passed before my last two edits (a lint fix to `fetch.py` and an `ruff --fix` import reorder in `settings.py`), and I haven't re-run it since. I also never ran the full backend suite. A quick check that a bad proxy mode falls back to `always` and that a bad URL is rejected was blocked by a permission prompt, so it didn't run.

- **Settings:** the four `SCRAPER_*` settings are in `mealie/core/settings/settings.py`, along with `ScraperProxyMode`. Unknown modes fall back to `always`. An empty URL is treated as unset, which the spec didn't say either way. A URL without a scheme and host fails validation.
- **`fetch` module:** `mealie/pkgs/safehttp/fetch.py` has `resilient_fetch` and the challenge helpers, following the rotation, proxy, wait and FlareSolverr rules in your spec.
- **`ForceTimeoutException`:** I moved it into `fetch.py` and re-imported it in `scraper_strategies.py`, so the recipe routes' import still works.
- **`flaresolverr` module:** `mealie/pkgs/safehttp/flaresolverr.py` has `FlareSolverrSolution` and `solve`. `solve` returns `None` on any failure and never raises.
- **URL imports:** `safe_scrape_html`, the HEAD size probe and image downloads in `recipe_data_service.py` now all go through `resilient_fetch`. Image downloads pass `allow_flaresolverr=False`. The size probe uses `method="HEAD"`.

I left `ruff check` clean on `mealie`.

+import asyncio
+import random
+import time
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import httpx
+from httpx import AsyncClient
+
+from mealie.core.config import get_app_settings
+from mealie.core.root_logger import get_logger
+from mealie.core.settings.settings import ScraperProxyMode
+
+from . import flaresolverr
+from .transport import AsyncSafeTransport
+
+__all__ = [
+    "BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS",
+    "FetchResult",
+    "ForceTimeoutException",
+    "ScraperProxyMode",
+    "body_indicates_challenge",
+    "flaresolverr",
+    "headers_indicate_challenge",
+    "is_challenge_status",
+    "resilient_fetch",
+]
+
+logger = get_logger()
+
+BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS = [
+    "chrome",
+    "firefox",
+    "safari",
+    "edge",
+]
+
+_CHALLENGE_BODY_SAMPLE = 4096
+_CHALLENGE_MARKERS = (
+    b"__cf_chl",
+    b"cf-browser-verification",
+    b"/cdn-cgi/challenge-platform",
+    b"datadome",
+)
+
+_OVERALL_BUDGET = 45.0
+_DEFAULT_RETRY_WAIT = 1.0
+_MAX_RETRY_WAIT = 5.0
+_MAX_JITTER = 0.5
+
+
+class ForceTimeoutException(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FetchResult:
+    content: bytes
+    status_code: int
+    url: str
+    headers: httpx.Headers
+    encoding: str | None
+
+    @property
+    def text(self) -> str:
+        try:
+            return str(self.content, self.encoding, errors="replace")  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+        except (LookupError, TypeError):
+            # unknown encoding name, or no encoding at all
+            return str(self.content, errors="replace")
+
+
+def is_challenge_status(status_code: int) -> bool:
+    if status_code == 503:
+        return True
+    return 400 <= status_code < 500 and status_code not in (404, 410)
+
+
+def headers_indicate_challenge(headers: httpx.Headers) -> bool:
+    return "cf-mitigated" in headers
+
+
+def body_indicates_challenge(content: bytes) -> bool:
+    sample = content[:_CHALLENGE_BODY_SAMPLE].lower()
+    return any(marker in sample for marker in _CHALLENGE_MARKERS)
+
+
+def _build_transport(impersonate: str, proxy: str | None = None) -> AsyncSafeTransport:
+    kwargs = {}
+    if proxy:
+        kwargs["proxy"] = proxy
+    return AsyncSafeTransport(
+        impersonate=impersonate,
+        default_headers=True,
+        verify=False,  # disable SSL verification since we can handle untrusted data and some sites don't have certs
+        **kwargs,
+    )
+
+
+def _retry_wait(headers: httpx.Headers) -> float:
+    wait = _DEFAULT_RETRY_WAIT
+    try:
+        parsed = float(headers.get("retry-after", ""))
+        if parsed >= 0:
+            wait = parsed
+    except ValueError:
+        pass
+    return min(wait, _MAX_RETRY_WAIT) + random.uniform(0, _MAX_JITTER)
+
+
+class _Blocked(Exception):
+    def __init__(self, wait: bool, headers: httpx.Headers):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.wait = wait
+        self.headers = headers
+
+
+class _HardError(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+async def _attempt(url: str, method: str, timeout: int, impersonate: str, proxy: str | None) -> FetchResult:
+    transport = _build_transport(impersonate, proxy)
+    async with AsyncClient(transport=transport) as client:
+        async with client.stream(method, url, timeout=timeout, follow_redirects=True) as resp:
+            status = resp.status_code
+            headers = resp.headers
+
+            if is_challenge_status(status) or headers_indicate_challenge(headers):
+                raise _Blocked(status in (429, 503), headers)
+
+            if status >= 400:
+                raise _HardError(status)
+
+            content = b""
+            if method.upper() != "HEAD":
+                start = time.time()
+                async for chunk in resp.aiter_bytes(chunk_size=1024):
+                    content += chunk
+                    if time.time() - start > timeout:
+                        raise ForceTimeoutException()
+
+                if body_indicates_challenge(content):
+                    raise _Blocked(False, headers)
+
+            return FetchResult(content, status, str(resp.url), headers, resp.encoding)
+
+
+async def resilient_fetch(
+    url: str,
+    *,
+    method: str = "GET",
+    timeout: int = 15,
+    allow_flaresolverr: bool = True,
+) -> FetchResult | None:
+    """
+    Fetch a url, rotating browser TLS impersonations (and optionally a proxy), then falling back to
+    FlareSolverr, to get past bot protection. Returns None if the page could not be fetched.
+    """
+    settings = get_app_settings()
+    proxy_url = settings.SCRAPER_PROXY_URL
+    flaresolverr_url = settings.SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_URL
+
+    rotations: list[str | None]
+    if not proxy_url:
+        rotations = [None]
+    elif settings.SCRAPER_PROXY_MODE == ScraperProxyMode.FALLBACK:
+        rotations = [None, proxy_url]
+    else:
+        rotations = [proxy_url]
+
+    plan: list[tuple[str, str | None]] = []
+    for proxy in rotations:
+        order = list(BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS)
+        random.shuffle(order)
+        plan.extend((imp, proxy) for imp in order)
+
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + _OVERALL_BUDGET
+
+    for i, (impersonation, proxy) in enumerate(plan):
+        if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
+            break
+
+        logger.debug(f'Trying browser impersonation: "{impersonation}" (proxy: {bool(proxy)})')
+        try:
+            return await _attempt(url, method, timeout, impersonation, proxy)
+        except _HardError as e:
+            logger.debug(f'Error status code {e} with impersonation "{impersonation}"')
+            return None
+        except _Blocked as e:
+            logger.debug(f'Blocked with impersonation "{impersonation}"')
+            if e.wait and i + 1 < len(plan):
+                await asyncio.sleep(_retry_wait(e.headers))
+
+    if flaresolverr_url and allow_flaresolverr and method.upper() != "HEAD":
+        solution = await flaresolverr.solve(flaresolverr_url, url, settings.SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_TIMEOUT)
+        if solution is None:
+            return None
+        return FetchResult(
+            solution.html.encode("utf-8"),
+            solution.status_code,
+            solution.url,
+            httpx.Headers({"content-type": "text/html; charset=utf-8"}),
+            "utf-8",
+        )
+
+    return None

+    cookies: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
+    user_agent: str = ""
+
+
+async def solve(base_url: str, url: str, timeout: int) -> FlareSolverrSolution | None:
+    """
+    Ask a FlareSolverr instance to load `url` in a real browser and return the solved page.
+    Never raises; returns None on any failure.
+    """
+    endpoint = base_url.rstrip("/") + "/v1"
+    payload = {"cmd": "request.get", "url": url, "maxTimeout": int(timeout * 1000)}
+
+    try:
+        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=timeout + 15) as client:
+            response = await client.post(endpoint, json=payload)
+            if response.status_code != 200:
+                logger.debug("FlareSolverr returned HTTP %s", response.status_code)
+                return None
+            data = response.json()
+
+        if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("status") != "ok":
+            logger.debug("FlareSolverr did not report success")
+            return None
+
+        solution = data.get("solution")
+        if not isinstance(solution, dict) or not solution.get("response"):
+            return None
+
+        return FlareSolverrSolution(
+            html=solution["response"],
+            status_code=solution.get("status", 200),
+            url=solution.get("url") or url,
+            cookies=solution.get("cookies") or [],
+            user_agent=solution.get("userAgent") or "",
+        )
+    except Exception as e:
+        logger.debug("FlareSolverr request failed: %s", e)
+        return None

+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Any
+
+import httpx
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FlareSolverrSolution:
+    html: str
+    status_code: int
+    url: str
+    cookies: list[Any] = field(default_factory=list)
+    user_agent: str = ""
+
+
+async def solve(base_url: str, url: str, timeout: int) -> FlareSolverrSolution | None:
+    """Ask a FlareSolverr instance to load `url`. Returns None on any failure."""
+    endpoint = base_url.rstrip("/") + "/v1"
+    payload = {"cmd": "request.get", "url": url, "maxTimeout": int(timeout * 1000)}
+
+    try:
+        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=timeout + 15) as client:
+            resp = await client.post(endpoint, json=payload)
+            if resp.status_code != 200:
+                return None
+
+            data = resp.json()
+            if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("status") != "ok":
+                return None
+
+            solution = data.get("solution")
+            if not isinstance(solution, dict) or not solution.get("response"):
+                return None
+
+            return FlareSolverrSolution(
+                html=solution["response"],
+                status_code=solution.get("status") or 200,
+                url=solution.get("url") or url,
+                cookies=solution.get("cookies") or [],
+                user_agent=solution.get("userAgent") or "",
+            )
+    except Exception:
+        return None

usage.answer:
Resilient fetching is in, with the optional proxy and FlareSolverr support. The unit suite passes; I didn't run the full backend suite, and I didn't write any tests for the new code.

I also didn't exercise `resilient_fetch` against a real server or the proxy path. The new fetch and FlareSolverr code has only been exercised through the existing tests.

- **Settings:** the four `SCRAPER_*` settings, the `ScraperProxyMode` enum (unknown values fall back to `always`) and the URL validation are in `mealie/core/settings/settings.py`. I spot-checked the validator on the accepted and rejected examples from your spec, and it behaved as specified. An empty string is treated the same as unset.
- **`mealie/pkgs/safehttp/fetch.py`:** this holds the challenge detectors, `FetchResult`, `_build_transport` and `resilient_fetch`. It covers rotation, proxy modes, the `Retry-After` wait, the 45-second budget, hard errors and the FlareSolverr last resort.
- **`mealie/pkgs/safehttp/flaresolverr.py`:** `solve` and `FlareSolverrSolution` are there.
- **`ForceTimeoutException`:** it is now defined in `fetch.py` and re-exported from `scraper_strategies.py`, so the recipe routes' import still works.
- **Callers:** `safe_scrape_html` now calls `resilient_fetch`. Image downloads pass `allow_flaresolverr=False`. The largest-image size probe uses `method="HEAD"`. A page that can't be fetched still returns `""` and an image that can't be fetched is still skipped.
- **Image download change:** images now go through the rotation, so the first impersonation is no longer always `chrome` as it was.

On the first unit-test run, `test_pagination_total_calculation` failed with a read-only database error. A second pytest run was going in the background at the time. A clean rerun passed.

+import asyncio
+import logging
+import random
+import time
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import httpx
+from httpx import AsyncClient
+
+from mealie.core.config import get_app_settings
+from mealie.core.settings.settings import ScraperProxyMode
+
+from . import flaresolverr
+from .transport import AsyncSafeTransport
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+__all__ = [
+    "BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS",
+    "FetchResult",
+    "ForceTimeoutException",
+    "ScraperProxyMode",
+    "body_indicates_challenge",
+    "flaresolverr",
+    "headers_indicate_challenge",
+    "is_challenge_status",
+    "resilient_fetch",
+]
+
+BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS = [
+    "chrome",
+    "firefox",
+    "safari",
+    "edge",
+]
+
+_CHALLENGE_BODY_SAMPLE = 4096
+_CHALLENGE_MARKERS = [
+    b"__cf_chl",
+    b"cf-browser-verification",
+    b"/cdn-cgi/challenge-platform",
+    b"datadome",
+    b"_incapsula_resource",
+    b"px-captcha",
+]
+
+_OVERALL_BUDGET = 45.0
+_DEFAULT_RETRY_WAIT = 1.0
+_MAX_RETRY_WAIT = 5.0
+_MAX_JITTER = 0.25
+
+
+class ForceTimeoutException(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+def is_challenge_status(status_code: int) -> bool:
+    if status_code == 503:
+        return True
+    return 400 <= status_code < 500 and status_code not in (404, 410)
+
+
+def headers_indicate_challenge(headers: httpx.Headers) -> bool:
+    return "cf-mitigated" in headers
+
+
+def body_indicates_challenge(content: bytes) -> bool:
+    sample = content[:_CHALLENGE_BODY_SAMPLE].lower()
+    return any(marker in sample for marker in _CHALLENGE_MARKERS)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FetchResult:
+    content: bytes
+    status_code: int
+    url: str
+    headers: httpx.Headers
+    encoding: str | None
+
+    @property
+    def text(self) -> str:
+        try:
+            return str(self.content, self.encoding, errors="replace")  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+        except (LookupError, TypeError):
+            # unknown encoding name, or no encoding at all; decode blindly
+            return str(self.content, errors="replace")
+
+
+def _build_transport(impersonate: str, proxy: str | None = None) -> AsyncSafeTransport:
+    kwargs = {}
+    if proxy:
+        kwargs["proxy"] = proxy
+
+    return AsyncSafeTransport(
+        impersonate=impersonate,
+        default_headers=True,
+        verify=False,  # disable SSL verification since we can handle untrusted data and some sites don't have certs
+        **kwargs,
+    )
+
+
+def _retry_wait(headers: httpx.Headers) -> float:
+    wait = _DEFAULT_RETRY_WAIT
+    try:
+        wait = float(headers.get("retry-after", ""))
+    except ValueError:
+        pass
+    if wait < 0:
+        wait = _DEFAULT_RETRY_WAIT
+    return min(wait, _MAX_RETRY_WAIT) + random.uniform(0, _MAX_JITTER)
+
+
+async def resilient_fetch(
+    url: str,
+    *,
+    method: str = "GET",
+    timeout: int = 15,
+    allow_flaresolverr: bool = True,
+) -> FetchResult | None:
+    """
+    Fetch a url, rotating browser TLS impersonations (and optionally a proxy) past bot protection.
+    A FlareSolverr instance is used as a last resort for bodies. Returns None when the url cannot be fetched.
+    """
+    settings = get_app_settings()
+    proxy_url = settings.SCRAPER_PROXY_URL
+    proxy_mode = settings.SCRAPER_PROXY_MODE
+
+    if not proxy_url:
+        rotations: list[str | None] = [None]
+    elif proxy_mode == ScraperProxyMode.FALLBACK:
+        rotations = [None, proxy_url]
+    else:
+        rotations = [proxy_url]
+
+    plan: list[tuple[str, str | None]] = []
+    for proxy in rotations:
+        order = list(BROWSER_IMPERSONATIONS)
+        random.shuffle(order)
+        plan.extend((imp, proxy) for imp in order)
+
+    reads_body = method.upper() != "HEAD"
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + _OVERALL_BUDGET
+
+    for i, (impersonation, proxy) in enumerate(plan):
+        if i > 0 and time.monotonic() >= deadline:
+            break
+
+        logger.debug(f'Trying browser impersonation: "{impersonation}" (proxied: {bool(proxy)})')
+
+        transport = _build_transport(impersonation, proxy)
+        async with AsyncClient(transport=transport) as client:
+            async with client.stream(method, url, timeout=timeout, follow_redirects=True) as resp:
+                status_code = resp.status_code
+                headers = resp.headers
+
+                blocked = is_challenge_status(status_code) or headers_indicate_challenge(headers)
+
+                if not blocked and status_code >= 400:
+                    logger.debug(f'Error status code {status_code} with impersonation "{impersonation}"')
+                    return None
+
+                content = b""
+                if not blocked and reads_body:
+                    start_time = time.time()
+                    async for chunk in resp.aiter_bytes():
+                        content += chunk
+                        if time.time() - start_time > timeout:
+                            raise ForceTimeoutException()
+
+                    blocked = body_indicates_challenge(content)
+
+                if not blocked:
+                    return FetchResult(content, status_code, str(resp.url), headers, resp.encoding)
+
+        logger.debug(f'Blocked (status {status_code}) with impersonation "{impersonation}"')
+
+        if status_code in (429, 503) and i + 1 < len(plan):
+            await asyncio.sleep(_retry_wait(headers))
+
+    flaresolverr_url = settings.SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_URL
+    if flaresolverr_url and reads_body and allow_flaresolverr:
+        solution = await flaresolverr.solve(flaresolverr_url, url, settings.SCRAPER_FLARESOLVERR_TIMEOUT)
+        if solution is None:
+            return None
+
+        return FetchResult(
+            solution.html.encode("utf-8"),
+            solution.status_code,
+            solution.url,
+            httpx.Headers({"content-type": "text/html; charset=utf-8"}),
+            "utf-8",
+        )
+
+    return None

+import logging
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Any
+
+import httpx
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FlareSolverrSolution:
+    html: str
+    status_code: int
+    url: str
+    cookies: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
+    user_agent: str = ""
+
+
+async def solve(base_url: str, url: str, timeout: int) -> FlareSolverrSolution | None:
+    """
+    Ask a FlareSolverr instance to load `url` in a real browser and return the solved page.
+    Never raises; returns None on any failure.
+    """
+    endpoint = f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1"
+    payload = {"cmd": "request.get", "url": url, "maxTimeout": int(timeout * 1000)}
+
+    try:
+        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=timeout + 15) as client:
+            response = await client.post(endpoint, json=payload)
+            if response.status_code != 200:
+                logger.debug(f"FlareSolverr returned HTTP {response.status_code}")
+                return None
+            data = response.json()
+
+        if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("status") != "ok":
+            logger.debug("FlareSolverr did not solve the request")
+            return None
+
+        solution = data.get("solution")
+        if not isinstance(solution, dict) or not solution.get("response"):
+            return None
+
+        return FlareSolverrSolution(
+            html=solution["response"],
+            status_code=solution.get("status", 200),
+            url=solution.get("url") or url,
+            cookies=solution.get("cookies") or [],
+            user_agent=solution.get("userAgent") or "",
+        )
+    except Exception as e:
+        logger.debug(f"FlareSolverr request failed: {e}")
+        return None

usage.answer:
The SSRF fixes are in place across scraping, webhooks, recipe actions and the OIDC avatar download. I haven't done the end-to-end check of the pin against a local server, and I haven't updated the OIDC provider tests.

- **Tests:** the safehttp unit tests and the household integration tests pass. I changed two of those integration tests to patch `safehttp.post` instead of `requests.post`. The old OIDC tests in `tests/unit_tests/core/security/providers/test_openid_provider.py` still fail, because they mock `requests.get` and `socket.getaddrinfo` against the old flow. They need rewriting against `SafeTransport`/`CurlTransport.handle_request`, and I haven't done that.
- **Not run:** ruff format and lint were blocked by the permission prompt, so run `task py:format` and `task py:lint`. I also haven't run the full backend suite or mypy.
- **Pin check:** I only spot-checked `is_blocked_ip` and `_validate`. They gave the expected results for 8.8.8.8, a public IP-literal URL, 169.254.169.254, 100.64.0.1 and `::ffff:127.0.0.1`.
- **NOPROXY:** with no proxy it is `"*"`, with a proxy it is `""`, and applying a pin leaves it alone.

**What changed**
- **Settings:** `HTTP_ALLOW_LIST` and `HTTP_DISALLOW_LIST` are added to `AppSettings`, with the `http_allow_list` and `http_disallow_list` properties.
- **Transport:**
  - `mealie/pkgs/safehttp/transport.py` now has `is_blocked_ip`, a sync `SafeTransport` and `post`, all exported from the package.
  - `AsyncSafeTransport` and `SafeTransport` share the validation. Each request resolves the host, checks every address (deny list first, then the allow list, then the default block), and pins the checked addresses with `CurlOpt.RESOLVE` before calling the curl base class.
  - httpx-curl-cffi only keeps its `NOPROXY` option when the caller passes a non-empty `curl_options` dict, so both constructors seed one. Without that, `curl_options` stayed empty.
- **Callers:**
  - Webhooks and the post-type recipe action call `safehttp.post`, looking it up on the package each time. The recipe action goes through a small `_send_post` helper that adds the allow and deny lists.
  - `_build_transport` passes `allow_hosts` and `deny_hosts` from `get_app_settings()`.
- **OIDC avatar:**
  - The download goes through `SafeTransport`. The allow list is `HTTP_ALLOW_LIST` plus the provider's host, and the deny list is `HTTP_DISALLOW_LIST`.
  - Redirects are followed manually up to 3. Each hop is re-checked for the https rule, and its addresses are re-checked in the transport.
  - The Content-Length and streaming size caps are kept.

Configured proxies still resolve names themselves, so the pin can't hold there. That trade-off is as you described it.

The SSRF guards are in place and the new checks pass in a few spot-checks. The existing OIDC avatar tests and two integration tests now fail, because they mock the old `requests`/`socket` code. I haven't updated them or written new tests for the new behaviour.

**What I ran**
- The existing `tests/unit_tests/pkgs/safehttp` tests pass. ruff and mypy are clean.
- `is_blocked_ip` and the `_validate` return values: I only tried `https://93.184.216.34/`, which returns `None`. A `169.254.169.254` request is rejected.
- `post("http://127.0.0.1:1/")` raises `InvalidDomainError`.
- An `AsyncSafeTransport` with `allow_hosts=["pinned.example"]`, under a resolver answering 127.0.0.1, reached a local server and got 200 "OK". So the pin works.
- I didn't run the whole backend suite.

**What changed**
- **Settings:** `HTTP_ALLOW_LIST` and `HTTP_DISALLOW_LIST` are read from the environment and exposed as `http_allow_list` and `http_disallow_list`.
- **Transports:** `mealie/pkgs/safehttp/transport.py` now has `is_blocked_ip`, `_validate`, `_apply_pin`, a sync `SafeTransport` and `post`. Both transports check every request and redirect hop, then pin the connection to the checked addresses, and the deny list wins over the allow list. The package exports `SafeTransport`, `is_blocked_ip` and `post`.
- **Webhooks and recipe actions:** both send through `safehttp.post` and pick up the allow and deny lists. The recipe-action trigger looks `post` up on the package each time it sends.
- **Scraping:** `_build_transport` adds the two lists, read from `get_app_settings()` on each call.
- **OIDC avatar:** the download now goes through `SafeTransport`, with the allow list plus the provider's host and the deny list. I rewrote the redirect handling to follow redirects manually, up to 3. Each hop gets the https rule and the address check. The 5 MiB cap is checked against Content-Length and while streaming.

**Failing tests**
- 35 or so tests in `tests/unit_tests/core/security/providers/test_openid_provider.py` fail. They monkeypatch `requests.get` and `openid_provider.socket`, which no longer exist.
- `test_group_recipe_actions_trigger_post[False-False]` and `test_post_test_webhook` also fail, as they still patch `requests.post`.

I haven't confirmed that each of these failures comes only from the old mocks. The tests need updating to patch `socket.getaddrinfo`, `CurlTransport.handle_request` and `safehttp.post` instead; say if you want me to do that.

I've closed the SSRF and DNS rebinding holes, but I haven't updated the old tests, so 19 of them fail. I ran a smoke test and `ruff check`, and both passed. The smoke test confirmed that `safehttp.post` to `127.0.0.1` is blocked by default and returns 200 with `allow_hosts=["127.0.0.1"]`. I did not run the whole backend suite.

**Failing tests.** In the quick-loop run, 16 of the 19 are in `test_openid_provider.py`. The rest are `test_group_recipe_actions_trigger_post` and `test_post_test_webhook`. The few I checked fail because they patch `requests` or `requests.post`, which the new code no longer uses. They need rewriting to mock `CurlTransport.handle_request`, `socket.getaddrinfo` and `safehttp.post`. I didn't check whether every one fails for that reason.

**Not checked.** I haven't exercised the redirect, size-cap and avatar-storage cases, or the per-hop checks on redirects. I also haven't tested the scraper path or the new `_build_transport` arguments.

- **Settings** (`mealie/core/settings/settings.py`): added `HTTP_ALLOW_LIST` and `HTTP_DISALLOW_LIST`, exposed as `http_allow_list` and `http_disallow_list`.
- **Transport** (`mealie/pkgs/safehttp/transport.py`): added `is_blocked_ip`, `SafeTransport` and `post`, and rebuilt `AsyncSafeTransport`.
  - Before anything connects, `_validate` checks every request, including each redirect hop.
  - It resolves the name once and checks every address returned. The deny list is checked first, then the allow list, then the blocked-address rule.
  - It then pins those exact addresses into curl's RESOLVE option, so curl can't re-resolve the name.
  - With no explicit proxy, NOPROXY stays `*`, as before.
  - All of this is exported from the `safehttp` package.
- **Webhooks and recipe actions**: both now send through `safehttp.post`, looked up on the package at send time, with the allow and deny lists from settings. The recipe-action trigger's status codes are unchanged.
- **Scraper** (`mealie/pkgs/safehttp/fetch.py`): `_build_transport` passes `allow_hosts` and `deny_hosts`, reading settings each time it runs.
- **OIDC avatar** (`mealie/core/security/providers/openid_provider.py`):
  - The download uses `SafeTransport`.
  - The allow list is `HTTP_ALLOW_LIST` plus the provider's own host, and the deny list is `HTTP_DISALLOW_LIST`.
  - Redirects are followed manually, up to `MAX_PICTURE_REDIRECTS`. Each hop re-applies the https rule, and `SafeTransport` rechecks its addresses.
  - An empty `Location` counts as the same URL, and `Content-Length` and streamed-size caps still apply.
  - Any failure skips the avatar without failing login.

+import http.server
+import ipaddress
+import socket
+import threading
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+
+import pytest
+
+from mealie.pkgs import safehttp
+
+
+class _Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_POST(self):
+        self.send_response(200)
+        self.send_header("Content-Length", "2")
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(b"OK")
+
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def local_server() -> Iterator[int]:
+    server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), _Handler)
+    threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
+    yield server.server_port
+    server.shutdown()
+    server.server_close()
+
+
+def test_post_blocks_loopback_by_default(local_server: int):
+    with pytest.raises(safehttp.InvalidDomainError):
+        safehttp.post(f"http://127.0.0.1:{local_server}/")
+
+
+def test_post_allows_listed_host(local_server: int):
+    assert safehttp.post(f"http://127.0.0.1:{local_server}/", allow_hosts=["127.0.0.1"]).status_code == 200
+
+
+def test_post_pins_resolved_address(local_server: int, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch):
+    real = socket.getaddrinfo
+
+    def fake(host, port, *args, **kwargs):
+        if host == "pinned.example":
+            return [(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM, 6, "", ("127.0.0.1", port))]
+        return real(host, port, *args, **kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(socket, "getaddrinfo", fake)
+    response = safehttp.post(f"http://pinned.example:{local_server}/", allow_hosts=["pinned.example"])
+    assert (response.status_code, response.text) == (200, "OK")
